locator: The street-and-number section, INDIANA AVENUE: the odd numbers 1619 (Dr. & Mrs. E. C. Dudley, Miss Katherine Dudley, John H. Dudley), 1623 (Mr. & Mrs. Murry Nelson), 1641 (Mrs. C. R. Cummings, Mrs. H. T. Robinson), 1703 and 1713; line 21874 onward in the item's OCR text. Also (T-3013): The Indiana Avenue street list (printed page 156): '2001 Mr. & Mrs. A. Courtney Campbell' (the OCR reads the number 2061; the alphabetical list prints 'Campbell A. Courtney, 2001 Indiana av.') and '2001 Mrs. George C. Morton'; '2125 Mr. & Mrs. Ira O. Bane', '2125 D. H. Bane'. The classified business list, 'Livery and Boarding Stables': 'BANE BROS. 2125 to 2129 Indiana av. Tels. South-338 and 405'. A display advertisement in the back matter: 'Bane Brothers' Livery, 2125, 2127 and 2129 Indiana Ave., Chicago, Ill., Phone South-405, Stylish Turnouts'. Also (T-3011): the same Indiana Avenue street list's east-side numbers between 18th and 20th Street (item OCR lines 24563-24597): 1813 (three households), 1815, 1819, 1821, 1825, 1829, 1833 (two), 1901, 1921 and 1933. For T-3154: nobody at 1925-1929, 1935-1937 or 216 E. 20th; Judge Marcus Kavanagh on Michigan Avenue (the series has him there from 1903 to 1908, at the Hotel Metropole in 1909, the Congress hotel in 1910 and 216 E. 20th only in 1911). Also (T-3253): the PRAIRIE AV. street list, printed pp. 186-187 (scan leaves 188-189), odd numbers 1619-2123 and even numbers 1600-2140, read whole for the 1904 Prairie Avenue household cards. Also (T-3266): the PRAIRIE AVENUE street list and the alphabetical list's Prairie Avenue lines, numbers 1600-2140, read again for who lived in each house before and after 1904 (docs/RESEARCH/prairie-former-residents-3266/).
rights_note: A US directory published in 1903, in the public domain. Read for who lived at an address; no asset is derived from it.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-24 (T-3068) from the item's OCR text (chicagobluebooko1904chic_djvu.txt), checked against the 1890, 1894, 1898 and 1901-1911 editions of the same series (items chicagobluebooko<year>chic), whose Indiana Avenue sections carry the same households at 1619 (Dudley, 1890-1908) and 1641 (Cummings and Robinson, 1890-1908). Read again 2026-10-23 for T-3013 (2001-2129 Indiana and the classified livery list) from the same OCR text, which is clean in those lines. Read again 2026-10-25 for T-3011 (Indiana Avenue 1801-1999, the east face of the 18th-20th block) from the same OCR text through archive.org's stream view; the lines are clean. Read again 2026-10-30 for T-3253 (Prairie Avenue 1600-2140) from the item's OCR through the BookReader page text and full-text search, not the page images: the page text of leaf 188 stops short of its last three lines (1808-1816), which the search supplied. The reading agrees entry for entry with the Prairie library's independent reading of the same OCR (chicago/prairie_1904_v1/data/occupancy_candidates.csv, 73 addresses). One surname is uncertain: 2123 'Hubbart' (the 1905 OCR reads 'Hulbert').
note: The Blue Book lists selected households only, so a number it omits is not thereby empty. What it does give is a dated household AT a number: on Indiana Avenue's east side, 16th to 18th Street, the 1904 edition lists 1619, 1623, 1641, 1703 and 1713, and nobody at 1601-1613, 1637 or 1727-1737. Further south it puts two households in 2001 Indiana Avenue and Bane Brothers' livery and boarding stables across 2125, 2127 and 2129 Indiana Avenue (classified list and a back-matter advertisement). On the east side from 18th to 20th Street (T-3011) it lists ten numbers, 1813 to 1833 and 1901, 1921 and 1933, and nobody at 1801-1811, 1835-1899 or the other 1900s. On Prairie Avenue (T-3253) it is the base of every 1904 household card from 1600 to 2140: it prints married couples as 'Mr. & Mrs.', unmarried daughters only as '& dr.' or '& drs.', grown sons and other adults by name, and no young children and no servants.
